clue.text: Employment concession in the Midlands

definitions.note: a phrase describing a place, standing for the town's name

parts.note: employment is work, a job
a sop is a small concession made to placate someone

explanation.surface: A job perk granted somewhere in central England.
explanation.walkthrough: WORKSOP is a market town in Nottinghamshire, in England's East Midlands; the definition only says where it lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The town lies in Nottinghamshire, a county of England's East Midlands region.

clue.text: Rolls with gold finish for the royal family

parts.note: rolls up, as a reel does, means winds
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A gold-trimmed Rolls-Royce fit for royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' looks like the car but is the verb, winding something up.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor has been the British royal house's surname since 1917.

clue.text: Bond hit the drink

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
port is a fortified wine, a drink

explanation.surface: James Bond knocks back a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A close understanding between people is a bond between them.

clue.text: Gather under a quarter row

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece sits below the first

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass
to cull is to gather or pick out

explanation.surface: Someone gathering things during a squabble over a quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is the verb for propelling a boat with oars.
explanation.definitionFit: To scull is to propel a boat with oars, which is rowing.

clue.text: Where one may reflect over the water?

definitions.text: Where one may reflect over the water?

parts.words: Where one may reflect over the water?
parts.note: reads as a spot on a jetty for musing, but means a tall mirror once hung between windows

explanation.surface: A quiet spot on a jetty for contemplation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall mirror hung on the wall section between windows is where people see their reflection.

clue.text: Ring about tot going on foot

indicators.note: the ring word goes round, about, the tot word

parts.note: a ping is a ringing sound
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A ring around a small child out walking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a toddler but is the verb, adding up.
explanation.definitionFit: To pad is to walk softly, so padding is travelling on foot.

clue.text: Object to pin being used

indicators.note: the letters of 'to pin' are put to use in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone objecting to a pin being put to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb of protest but is the noun, a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: The object of an exercise is its purpose or aim.

clue.text: Meat of a sort is indeed supplied

indicators.note: the meat word is set in the deed, reading 'indeed' as 'in deed'

parts.note: split as 'in deed': a deed is a legal document
liver is a kind of offal eaten as meat

explanation.surface: A butcher insists the meat really was handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'indeed' as 'in deed': LIVER goes in DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods supplied to a customer have been handed over, brought to them.

clue.text: Letter opening

definitions.meaning: a first letter of a name, as on a monogram

explanation.definitionFit: A capital at the start of a name, or anything coming first at the beginning.

clue.text: Indigent theatre-goers, all packed into grey convertible

indicators.note: the word all is stuffed inside the grey letters
the letters of grey can be converted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Poor playgoers cram into a grey open-topped car.
explanation.walkthrough: The gallery, or 'the gods', is the cheapest, highest seating in a theatre, so the word also means the people sitting there.
explanation.definitionFit: The top balcony of cheap seats, and the poorer audience members who fill it.

clue.text: The main supervisor

parts.note: reads as a chief overseer, but main means the sea, so this is the Roman god ruling it

explanation.surface: A head manager at work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of the sea, the 'main' in old poetic usage, rules over the oceans.

clue.text: Invalid legal document causing a certain acrimony

parts.note: someone invalid, sickly, is ill
a will is a legal document leaving property

explanation.surface: A disputed testament breeds bitterness in a family.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility or malice towards someone is a form of acrimony.

clue.text: A warning culminating in insult

indicators.note: the culminating word sits inside the insult word

parts.note: a slight is an insult or snub
top, as an adjective, means highest or culminating

explanation.surface: A caution that ends with an affront.
explanation.definitionFit: A red traffic signal warns drivers to halt.

clue.text: "Give every man thine ear, but few thy — " Shakespeare (Hamlet)

definitions.text: "Give every man thine ear, but few thy — " Shakespeare (Hamlet)

parts.words: "Give every man thine ear, but few thy — " Shakespeare (Hamlet)
parts.note: Polonius advises his son Laertes to listen to all but speak to few; the missing word is the one for speech

explanation.surface: A line of Polonius's advice to Laertes with its last word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Polonius's advice contrasts listening with speaking, so the missing word means one's spoken opinion.

clue.text: The painter meeting setback makes charges

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, stands for a painter
read as 'set back': the word set written backwards

explanation.surface: An artist suffers a reverse and bills the client.
explanation.walkthrough: RA means a Royal Academician, a painter. Read 'setback' as 'set back', SET reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices asked for goods or services are charges.

clue.text: Beginning to accept the left can be most unexpected

indicators.note: the beginning word takes in, accepts, the letter for left

parts.note: starting means beginning
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Taking up left-wing politics can be a surprising start.
explanation.definitionFit: Something startling is so surprising that it gives a jolt.

clue.text: A trim lady reorganised the naval office

indicators.note: the letters of 'A trim lady' are organised again in a new order

explanation.surface: A tidy woman tidied up the navy's headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: The ADMIRALTY was the British government department running the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: The department that commanded the British navy was this office.

clue.text: Lone mites abandoned at the roadside

indicators.note: left unrestrained, the letters of 'Lone mites' run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Tiny insects left on their own beside a road.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition says where the answer is found: a stone marking distances by a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A post marking the distance along a road stands by the verge.

clue.text: Listens in sure enough for practice

indicators.note: the listening word goes inside the word for sure enough

parts.note: real, as in 'for real', means genuine, sure enough
hears means listens

explanation.surface: Someone listens in, confident of the tune, at a run-through.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial performance before the real one is practice for it.

clue.text: Dress in a bright colour when finished work

indicators.note: the dress word sits inside the colour word

parts.note: red is a bright colour
tire is an old word for attire or dress

explanation.surface: Someone dons a vivid outfit on leaving the job.
explanation.walkthrough: TIRE, short for attire, is an archaic word for dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone retired has stopped working at the end of a career.

clue.text: Leaves luggage in this place

indicators.note: the luggage word sits inside the place word

parts.note: here means this place
a bag is a piece of luggage

explanation.surface: Someone departs and leaves their luggage behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb of departing; it is the noun, foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass and green foliage are herbage.

clue.text: Little notes written about a fight

indicators.note: the two notes are written round the fight word

parts.note: D and F are musical notes
a war is a fight

explanation.surface: A few musical notes jotted down about a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stunted and undersized is little.

clue.text: A worker consuming fruit for sustenance

indicators.note: the worker swallows, consumes, the fruit word

parts.note: an ant, as in worker ant
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A labourer eats fruit to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that nourishes is sustenance.

clue.text: Punishes two ways-that's cunning

parts.note: fines means punishes with a money penalty
S and E, south and east, are two compass directions

explanation.surface: Penalising people in two ways is crafty.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill and subtlety in handling a situation, a kind of cunning.

clue.text: The sailor turned to is a card!

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: the little word to is turned round

explanation.surface: An old sea dog is quite a character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' looks like a jolly fellow, an eccentric, but is a fortune-teller's card.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the fortune-teller's pack is a picture card.

clue.text: Figure Italians upset Spanish

parts.note: C is the Roman figure for 100

indicators.note: the letters of Italians are upset into a new order

explanation.surface: A statue that upset Italians is of a Spaniard.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard Spanish comes from the old kingdom of Castile.

clue.text: Understood about a Shakespearean role

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
King Lear is the title role of one of Shakespeare's plays

explanation.surface: Someone grasped a Shakespeare part.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear meaning is easily understood.

clue.text: Pointless though popular Oriental exercise

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
E stands for Eastern
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A trendy Eastern workout is a waste of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy and ineffectual is lacking point, so pointless.

clue.text: Convert assets into cash. Get the idea?

definitions.meaning: to turn property into money by selling it

explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both: selling up assets for money, and coming to understand something.

clue.text: There's no sense in this agreement

indicators.note: says the letters of 'no sense' are found in this answer in another order

explanation.surface: An accord that makes no sense at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Unity of mind between people is agreement.

clue.text: A doctor should retain the right keenness — it makes a profound difference

indicators.note: the doctor's letters hold, retain, the next pieces inside

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
edge means sharpness or keenness

explanation.surface: Advice that a physician keep his edge to change things deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'profound' looks like 'great' but means deep: this vessel deepens channels.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that scoops silt from a riverbed makes the water deeper.

clue.text: Name label

definitions.meaning: to give a title to, name

explanation.definitionFit: Both mean giving something a title or designation.
